Maya (product): Heads up — FinCo wants a private pilot with a 99.95% latency SLO for interactive queries. Pilot target: 6 weeks. This conflicts with our planned quantized rollout + current prewarm budget. Need quick cross-team decision on scope and owners.

Sam (eng): Can we scope the pilot to lower qps? If we cap to ~20 rps we can avoid quant rollout and keep latency tight.

Priya (runtime): Important context: the unquantized model needs ~2x GPU memory. Without reserved slots we’ll get eviction/cold-KV cache which spikes tail latency. Also continuous-batching helps but only for steady traffic.

Alex (infra): Reserved GPU slots are doable but require a committed month + provisioning window. Also HSM/KMS for private requires infra+network config. Timeline depends on signed PO.

Jordan (security): HSM onboarding needs vendor paperwork and our compliance signoff — realistically ~4 weeks if we prioritize reviews. We can parallelize some steps but need customer attestation docs.

Zoe (sre): From SRE side: if we rely purely on autoscale cold-starts, the tail P99 will blow past SLO. Prewarm + KV priming required. Rough cost estimate for prewarm capacity ~ $4k/mo for pilot shape.

Sam (eng): So options: A) Keep full model, reserve capacity, prewarm, postpone quant. Predictable latency but higher infra commit. B) Ship quantized model to reduce memory and startup cost, but there’s a small quality risk and we need evals. C) Hybrid: route low-risk queries to quant model, heavy queries to full model via canary routing.

Priya (runtime): Quantization risk: on certain prompt patterns hallucination/score drift appears. We need a focused eval set from FinCo to measure delta. Canary + rollback is doable but requires routing changes and latency instrumentation.

Maya (product): Decision requested by EOD tomorrow so sales can ask FinCo for PO. Question list: 1) Can infra commit reserved slots if sales gets a 1-mo PO? 2) Security: can HSM review be expedited? 3) Runtime: can you run a 48h quant evaluation against a vetted eval set? 4) SRE: runbook/rollback ready?

Alex (infra): Infra can commit reserved slots once we have a 1-month PO. I can fast-track network and VPC provisioning. HSM certs need Jordan to greenlight security checklist.

Jordan (security): I can prioritize HSM review but need the customer SOC/Security questionnaire + contact for attestation. If Maya/SE can push those tonight, I’ll start.

Zoe (sre): I’ll draft a prewarm/runbook and simple SLAs for the pilot: prewarm job, KV cache priming procedure, latency dashboards (P50/P95/P99), and circuit-breaker thresholds. Need infra config + host reservations to finalize.

Priya (runtime): We can run a 48-hour quant eval. Deliverables: P95 latency, token throughput, hallucination delta on our eval prompts, and a small failure-case list. Will need FinCo sample prompts or a proxy set.

Sam (eng): I’ll scope engineering work: prewarm scheduler + canary routing. Rough ETA: 3 days to get infra config wired, 2 days to integrate routing and metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: created ticket #12345 "pilot-onboard-prioritization" assigned to Maya, Sam, Priya, Alex, Jordan, Zoe

Maya (product): Great. Action owners and short summary:
- Maya: collect customer docs + push for 1-mo PO (TODAY)
- Alex: reserved slot ETA / network/VPC provisioning
- Jordan: HSM security review (fast-track if docs arrive)
- Priya: quant 48h eval + metrics (start asap)
- Sam: infra + routing plan for prewarm/canary
- Zoe: prewarm runbook + rollback playbook

Maya (product): Reconvene tomorrow 10:00am PT to lock decision. If PO confirmed, route = Option A (reserve+prewarm). If not, lean hybrid canary with quant but only after Priya's eval.

Sam (eng): ok, will start infra tickets and canary design.

Priya (runtime): will kick off eval now. Will post results in #12345.

Alex (infra): will draft reservation cost and ETA in the ticket.

Jordan (security): will block time for review tomorrow morning — please DM the contact details.

Zoe (sre): will drop the runbook draft by EOD.

Maya (product): thanks team :thumbsup:

Sam (eng): +1
